newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: China's B share indices closed mixed in slow trade on Wednesday with market sentiment cautious, while the A share indices rose on a technical rebound, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index edged down 0.368 points or 0.59 percent to 62.013 points and Shenzhen's B index inched up 0.47 points or 0.33 percent to close at 142.45 points.
Brokers said most institutions remained on the sidelines waiting for fresh trading incentives.
"Market sentiment was affected by rumours that Beijing was drafting measures to effectively prevent bank funds from flowing into the A share market," a Shenzhen trader said.

Shanghai's B shares continued a correction on Tuesday with selling focused on shares likely to post poor 1996 results, while institutional support for property developer Lujiazui prevented the index from falling further, brokers said.
Lujiazui was today's second most active share, up $0.012 or 1.50 percent to $0.808 on volume of 2.0 million shares.
Industrial Sewing Machine was the biggest loser on talk of poor 1996 results, plunging $0.018 or 10 percent to its limit-down of $0.162 on volume of 30,000 shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was again the most active stock on profit-taking, falling $0.004 or 1.16 percent $0.338 on volume of 2.6 million shares.
Meanwhile, Shenzhen's B share market finished slightly higher with light buying seen in counters likely to post solid results for last year, brokers said.
Property developer China Vanke was the biggest B share gainer and rose HK$0.14 or 2.63 percent to HK$5.46 on thin volume of 2,699 shares.
Changan Automobile was the most active share on volume of 573,000 shares and inched down HK$0.01 to HK$4.48.
The A share markets in both Shanghai and Shenzhen closed up on technical rebounds following losses on Tuesday, brokers said.
Shanghai's A index rose 9.698 points or 1.02 percent to 956.959 and Shenzhen's A share index added 3.37 points or 1.00 percent to end at 341.88 points.
Trading company Liaoning Chengda was the Shanghai A share star on institutional buying, rising 1.29 yuan or 7.87 percent to 17.68 yuan on volume of 1.3 million shares.
On Shenzhen's A share market, power generator maker Mindong Electric surged 0.51 yuan or 8.43 percent to 6.56 yuan on speculative buying.
